raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Overview

Enable `FULL_DECODE_ONLY` and `FULL_AND_PIECEWISE` for DeepSeek-V4.1 PCP with fixed-length DSpark, on top of merged #59857 and #61994. This reuses MRV2's CUDA Graph framework instead of requiring eager execution for this configuration.

In the earlier matched four-H20, cached-64K experiment, enabling graphs reduced decode TPOT from **57.29 to 8.02 ms at C1 (7.14x)** and **57.44 to 17.98 ms at C32 (3.20x)**. These compare eager with graphs on the same patched code, not a fresh benchmark of the latest main. The smaller, subsequent communication optimization is reported separately below.

## Claims

- Preserve attention, compressor/indexer and bounded-replay buffer addresses across graph replays.
- Capture rank-local decode requests and both local prefill segments using the existing graph framework.
- Reuse gathered PCP positions across SWA builders and combine decode hidden-state restoration; retain the mixed-batch path.

## Validation

Four H20 GPUs, TP1/PCP4/EP4, fixed DSpark5, Humming MoE A8 (target attention projections use W8A16), APC and SWA bounded replay. Both benchmark arms include #61554's Engram sharing.

### Eager vs CUDA Graphs

| Concurrency | Eager TPOT (ms/token) | Graph TPOT (ms/token) | TPOT speedup | Eager steady tok/s | Graph steady tok/s |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 1 | 57.29 | 8.02 | 7.14x | 17.4 | 123.9 |
| 32 | 57.44 | 17.98 | 3.20x | 546.8 | 1,704.6 |
| 64 | 58.20 | 28.18 | 2.07x | 1,078.1 | 2,145.2 |
| 128 | 60.37 | 43.20 | 1.40x | 2,079.9 | 2,854.6 |

Same code/model/settings, `--enforce-eager` vs `FULL_AND_PIECEWISE`, `max-num-seqs=256`, 65,536 input tokens, 2,048 output limit and 99.90% prefix hits. Median of three batches after warmup; DSpark acceptance was about 28% in both arms, with zero preemptions. These measurements predate the communication optimization and latest main sync.

<details>
<summary>Measurement method and limitations</summary>

One public-report excerpt and analysis question was repeated at each concurrency. Client TPOT is `(last-token arrival - first-token arrival) / (output tokens - 1)`, taking the median across requests, then across three batches. Steady throughput uses native token-counter deltas while all requests are decoding. Actual concurrency was verified; client connection pools exceeded concurrency (graph 272, eager 144).

Graph ran first, then eager. Natural EOS was enabled, but all outputs reached the 2K cap, including thinking tokens. This is cached decode performance, not production traffic or completed-answer quality. Cold 64K TTFT was unchanged in a separate run (2.348/2.350 s).

</details>

### Correctness and Regression Coverage

- `FULL_AND_PIECEWISE`: full GSM8K **1229/1319 (93.18%)**; 14/14 semantic HTTP probes across 1K-64K prompts, prefix hits and changing batches. Actual FULL, PIECEWISE and eager fallback execution were observed.
- `FULL_DECODE_ONLY`: full GSM8K **1237/1319 (93.78%)**; 14/14 semantic probes and the two-GPU restoration test passed with `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error`.
- After the October 29 main sync, 162 targeted regressions passed. Full-model evaluations above predate that sync. CI adds one real two-GPU restoration test to an existing job.
- The October 31 follow-up fixes two CI override errors: FlashInfer and ROCm now accept and forward the base builder's `cache_positions` argument. **162 targeted regressions passed again on H20**, including real two-GPU hidden-state restoration with `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error`. This follow-up changes no kernels; it has not had a new full-model, SM100 or ROCm end-to-end run.

<details>
<summary>Test commands and model-evaluation scope</summary>

```bash
pytest -q tests/models/test_deepseek_v41_pcp.py::test_pcp_decode_restore_preserves_hidden_states
pytest -q tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_pcp_manager.py tests/models/test_deepseek_v41_replay_batch.py tests/models/test_deepseek_v41_decoder_replay_layers.py tests/v1/attention/test_indexer_deepseek_v4_slot_mapping.py
pre-commit run --files vllm/models/deepseek_v41/nvidia/flashinfer_sparse.py vllm/models/deepseek_v41/amd/rocm.py

lm_eval run --model local-completions \
  --model_args model=dsv41-pcp,base_url=http://127.0.0.1:8316/v1/completions,num_concurrent=64,tokenized_requests=False \
  --include_path /work/gsm8k-client/tasks --tasks gsm8k \
  --num_fewshot 5 --batch_size 1 --gen_kwargs temperature=0 \
  --log_samples --seed 12345 --output_path "$RESULTS"
```

Model evaluation: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017, lm-eval 0.4.13, official GSM8K v3 task with local dataset files, all 1,319 questions, 256-token generation cap, max context 131072, synchronous scheduling, compilation mode 0 and breakable CUDA graphs enabled. Latest full-model checks used a 32K batch-token limit and 64 sequences. GPU model validation covers EP4; non-EP has not had an end-to-end run. The existing capture regression fails before the graph fix and passes afterward.

Earlier eager/graph GSM8K runs scored 93.03%/93.18%, with mean server TPOT 44.56/21.12 ms and evaluation time 379.49/193.84 s. They used a 16K batch-token limit and 16 sequences, so they are not directly comparable with the latest 64-sequence run.

For the October 31 signature fix, an isolated method-contract check reproduced `unexpected keyword argument 'cache_positions'` before the fix and passed 10 forwarding/default-argument checks afterward. Backend dependencies were stubbed for this check; it is not hardware coverage. Local pre-commit hooks, including Ruff, formatting and mypy, passed on the changed files.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Additional communication optimization: approximately 3% lower estimated C1 verification-cycle time</summary>

This is a separate before/after comparison with graphs already enabled. Pre-FULL all-gathers fell **12 to 5**, and hidden-state gathers **4 to 1**. The estimated C1 verification cycle fell **18.59 to 18.04 ms**. Request-level TPOT gains are small and mixed; this does not close the low-concurrency gap to TP4.

Same runtime/settings, 16,384 input tokens, 512 forced output tokens, temperature 0, 99.61% prefix hits, zero preemptions. Three measured batches after warmup; mean [min-max] across batches:

| Concurrency | Before TPOT (ms) | After TPOT (ms) | Acceptance before / after |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 1 | 5.58 [5.17-6.36] | 5.51 [5.37-5.68] | 47.0% / 45.7% |
| 2 | 6.24 [5.96-6.50] | 6.26 [6.01-6.68] | 46.7% / 44.2% |
| 4 | 7.10 [6.84-7.38] | 6.81 [6.67-7.08] | 43.3% / 44.4% |
| 8 | 7.90 [7.69-8.04] | 7.82 [7.75-7.86] | 46.4% / 45.2% |
| 16 | 9.55 [9.41-9.70] | 9.64 [9.45-9.75] | 46.9% / 46.1% |
| 64 | 20.37 [19.94-20.74] | 20.47 [19.86-21.02] | 45.5% / 45.7% |

The cycle estimate divides streamed decode duration by native draft-round counts: before 18.588/18.602/18.573 ms, after 18.038/18.045/18.026 ms. It is not a direct engine timer. Separate eight-step traces verify collective counts; profiler timings are excluded. Inputs are repeated public text, not production requests.

</details>

## Details

Like #62377, this reuses the existing graph framework. V4.1 additionally needs persistent compressor/indexer metadata and replay KV slots/token IDs. Each SWA builder copies shared gathered positions into its capture-time buffer. Hidden-state packing is limited to decode batches with matching dtypes, preserving request order and avoiding extra prefill memory.

#64253 and #62749 explicitly exclude PCP; this PR does not duplicate their metadata kernels or capture mechanism. Engram sharing stays in #61554. Fixed-length DSpark is the scope here; adaptive verification and image-input support are separate work.

---

<details>
<summary>Pull Request Checklist</summary>

- [x] I used vLLM's `/pr-checklist` skill.
- [x] AI assistance was used during the creation of this PR.
- [x] **Design Fit:** Reuses the existing graph framework.
- [x] **Testing and Validation:** Regression, serving and model evaluation results and limits are listed above.
- [x] **Code Quality and Style:** The follow-up is limited to two override signatures and argument forwarding; local check results and limits are listed above.
- [x] **Pull Request Contents:** Design, measurements and limitations are described above.

</details>

@@ -16,6 +16,75 @@ Depending on the use case, there are two possible strategies:
 
 Both approaches are under active development.
 
+### DeepSeek-V4.1 CUDA graphs
+
+DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash supports PCP CUDA graphs on NVIDIA CUDA using Model Runner V2
+and `FLASHMLA_SPARSE_DSV41`. Select the graph mode explicitly:
+
+- `FULL_AND_PIECEWISE` uses full graphs for decode and breakable piecewise graphs
+  for prefill and mixed batches within the captured token sizes.
+- `FULL_DECODE_ONLY` uses full graphs for decode; prefill and mixed batches run
+  eagerly.
+- `NONE` disables CUDA graphs. Pure `FULL` and `PIECEWISE` modes are not
+  supported by this V4.1 PCP path.
+
+V4.1 uses breakable CUDA graphs rather than `torch.compile` graph splitting.
+Set `VLLM_USE_BREAKABLE_CUDAGRAPH=1` for piecewise modes. Compilation `mode=0`
+(`NONE`) disables `torch.compile`, not CUDA graphs: `cudagraph_mode` controls
+graph execution separately.
+
+For example, a four-GPU TP1/PCP4 instance with fixed-length DSpark can use:
+
+```bash
+VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1 VLLM_USE_BREAKABLE_CUDAGRAPH=1 \
+vllm serve deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017 \
+    --language-model-only --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v41 \
+    --tensor-parallel-size 1 --prefill-context-parallel-size 4 \
+    --enable-expert-parallel --all2all-backend allgather_reducescatter \
+    --attention-backend FLASHMLA_SPARSE_DSV41 \
+    --speculative-config '{"method":"dspark","num_speculative_tokens":5}' \
+    --max-model-len 32768 --max-num-seqs 32 --max-num-batched-tokens 4096 \
+    --enable-prefix-caching --swa-bounded-replay --no-async-scheduling \
+    --compilation-config '{"mode":0,"cudagraph_mode":"FULL_AND_PIECEWISE","cudagraph_capture_sizes":[5,6,10,12,20,24,40,48,80,96,160,192,256,512,768,1024],"max_cudagraph_capture_size":1024}' \
+    --cudagraph-metrics
+```
+
+Capture sizes are token counts. The example covers a 4096-token prefill split
+across PCP4 with 1024 tokens per rank, plus padded DSpark draft and verification
+buckets. Mixed and uneven batches can have larger local token counts; batches
+outside the captured sizes run eagerly. The draft processes the restored
+global batch, so do not divide its capture budget by the PCP size. Increase the
+capture sizes when increasing the batch-token limit. Use `--cudagraph-metrics`
+to check actual `FULL` and `PIECEWISE` execution counts; the configured mode
+alone does not prove either path ran.
+
+PCP gathers token positions once per batch for all SWA metadata groups. During
+decode, target and draft auxiliary hidden states with the same dtype share one
+gather before sampling. Each graph keeps its existing metadata buffers and
+request order; prefill hidden states continue to be restored separately.
+
+The example enables automatic prefix caching, which PCP bounded replay requires,
+and SWA bounded replay. Large
+piecewise graphs use an eager break to select the bounded decoder replay batch,
+then run its matching inner graph when available; larger replay batches fall
+back to eager execution. Keep `cudagraph_decoder_replay` enabled (the default)
+to retain bounded trimming in piecewise graphs. Full graphs and piecewise
+graphs below `decoder_replay_trim_threshold` keep the whole batch. Prefix-cache
+hits and bounded trimming depend on the requests and are not guaranteed by
+enabling the flags alone.
+
+Omit `--speculative-config` for ordinary decoding. PCP continues to require
+PP=DP=DCP=1, text-only input, synchronous scheduling, and no KV connector or
+MegaMoE. Adaptive speculative verification is unsupported. Engram tables remain
+TP-sharded and replicated across PCP ranks; account for their host memory when
+choosing the TP/PCP split.
+
+Speculative full-graph replay requires flattened or variable-length indexer queries,
+including when a PCP rank owns no decode requests. On SM90, fixed DSpark with
+5 speculative tokens uses the flattened path; native multi-query shapes such
+as 1 or 3 speculative tokens are rejected for graph execution. Use eager mode
+for those shapes.
+
 ## Decode Context Parallel
 
 Due to the auto-regressive nature of decoding, every decoding step needs to compute a small amount of query tokens w.r.t. a large number of key/value tokens stored in the paged KV cache. The core of decode context parallel is how to shard the KV cache across GPUs.

+accuracy_threshold: 0.88
+tolerance: 0.03
+min_acceptance_length: 2.5
+num_questions: 1319
+num_fewshot: 5

+max_concurrency: 17
+startup_max_wait_seconds: 1800

+# Capture 5/6-token DSpark buckets and PCP-local prefills up to 4096 / 4 tokens.
+server_args: >-
+  --revision 3431dde3247c13b5957f682b1e3c6fcae2566079
+  --language-model-only
+  --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v41
+  --trust-remote-code
+  --max-model-len 8192
+  --max-num-seqs 32
+  --max-num-batched-tokens 4096
+  --prefill-context-parallel-size 4
+  --enable-expert-parallel
+  --all2all-backend allgather_reducescatter
+  --speculative-config '{"method":"dspark","num_speculative_tokens":5}'
+  --compilation-config '{"mode":0,"cudagraph_mode":"FULL_AND_PIECEWISE","cudagraph_capture_sizes":[5,6,10,12,20,24,40,48,80,96,160,192,256,512,768,1024],"max_cudagraph_capture_size":1024}'
+  --enable-prefix-caching
+  --swa-bounded-replay
+  --cudagraph-metrics
+  --no-async-scheduling
+env:
+  VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER: "1"
